embedding.title: Embed papiro in a web app 🧩
embedding.text: Embed papiro in a web app 🧩 Papiro is also a library: it shows a wiki made by the papiro indexer inside any element of a page, for example the help of a web app. Every instance keeps its own pages, address and theme, and nothing outside its element is touched. Add the library Take papiro.js and papiro.css from the latest release , or use them from jsDelivr: <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/akrck02/papiro@lib/papiro.css" /> <script type="module"> import { createPapiro } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/akrck02/papiro@lib/papiro.js"; </script> papiro.js is an ES module with no dependencies. From TypeScript papiro-lib.tar.gz in the release (or the lib branch) has papiro.js , papiro.css and the type declarations ( papiro.d.ts and its folders). Copy them into your project, for example in src/lib/papiro/ , and import them as any module: import { createPapiro, type Papiro, type PapiroOptions } from "./lib/papiro/papiro.js"; const options: PapiroOptions = { source: "/wiki", layout: "page", route: "guides/settings" }; const help: Papiro = await createPapiro("#help", options); Options, layouts, themes and targets are typed, so a wrong value is a compile error. Show a wiki The wiki is the folder written by the papiro indexer ( index.json , the pages and their files). Give its url as source ; the instance takes the whole element, so give the element a size. import { createPapiro } from "./papiro.js"; const docs = await createPapiro("#docs", { source: "https://example.org/wiki", title: "Docs", hashPrefix: "docs", // the address is #/docs/wiki/…, the rest of the hash is the app's }); Layouts layout shows routing by default wiki bar, menu, search, pages and graph hash page only the pages, from route : help for one screen memory graph only the graph of the wiki memory // the help of a screen, links between pages still work const help = await createPapiro("#help", { source, layout: "page", route: "guides/settings" }); // a graph; the app decides what to do with the chosen page await createPapiro("#map", { source, layout: "graph", onNavigate: (target) => { if ("page" == target.view) help.navigate(target); }, }); Routing hash : the page is in the address, under hashPrefix ( #/docs/wiki/guides/settings ), so it can be shared and the back button works. Hashes outside the prefix belong to the app and are ignored. memory : the instance keeps the page and never touches the address. Options option default what it does source url of the indexed wiki layout wiki wiki , page or graph routing by layout hash or memory hashPrefix "" the section of the hash that belongs to papiro route "" first page with memory routing, "" is the first page title , description , logo the wiki name, its description and an svg logo url theme auto auto follows the system, or light , dark accent papiro's ochre the project's colour ( "#2BB3A3" ), adjusted for each theme so text reads well font system system , or papiro for its reading fonts width normal normal keeps a reading column, wide lets the pages take the whole width; readers switch it from the bar bar , menu , search , graph , breadcrumb by layout show or hide each part startPage false a start page with the title and description footer false true for the papiro credits, or html shortcuts false Ctrl K opens the search, Shift T switches the theme onNavigate , onThemeChange , onFontChange called on each change, for example to remember the theme The instance docs.navigate("guides/settings"); // or { view: "graph" } docs.setTheme("dark"); // "light", "dark" or "auto" docs.setFont("papiro"); docs.openSearch(); docs.destroy(); // removes it and stops listening Colours and fonts The simplest way to give papiro the colour of a project is the accent option: one colour, and papiro works out a variant that reads at 4.5:1 or more on the light and the dark theme, and the soft tint of highlights. Every style lives under the .papiro class, and it uses css variables that the app can change, for each theme: .papiro[data-theme="light"] { --primary-color: #2f6fd6; } .papiro[data-theme="dark"] { --primary-color: #8ab4ff; } .papiro { --font: "My font", sans-serif; --radius: 4px; } Some of them: --background , --surface-1 , --surface-2 , --text-color , --text-soft , --line , --primary-color , --primary-soft , --font , --font-reading , --font-console , --radius , the --code-* colours and the --graph-* colours. The layout follows the width of the element, not of the window: in a narrow element the bar goes to the bottom and the menu becomes a drawer. Example with three instances in one page

get-started.title: Getting started 🚀
get-started.text: Getting started 🚀 Getting started with papiro is very easy, right now there are 3 ways to set it up. Install papiro locally (recommended only for development or testing) Deploy as a github page Run it as a docker container Order of the pages Pages and folders are shown in alphabetical order. To choose the order, start their names with a number of one or two digits and a dash: 1-get-started.md , 2-installation/ , or 01-… , 02-… . The number only sets the position, it is not part of the address or the name ( #/wiki/get-started ), so links keep working. Pages without a number go after the numbered ones.

installation/docker.title: Use papiro as a docker container 🐳
installation/docker.text: Use papiro as a docker container 🐳 Papiro is published as a container image for amd64 and arm64: ghcr.io/akrck02/papiro . It indexes the documents in /resources/uploads , serves the wiki on port 8000 , and indexes them again a few seconds after they change. Obsidian vaults (a folder with .obsidian ) are detected. For the sake of simplicity we will use docker compose in this example, feel free to use whatever you prefer. services: papiro: container_name: papiro image: ghcr.io/akrck02/papiro:latest volumes: - ./my-documents:/resources/uploads environment: PAPIRO_TITLE: "My wiki" # the title of the wiki PAPIRO_WATCH_SECONDS: 5 # how often to look for changes, 0 to never ports: - 80:8000 restart: always Add your documents to the my-documents directory and start the container using: docker compose up Congratulations 🎉🎉 --- your wiki is now ready to visit in your domain running as a docker container. ---

installation/github-pages.title: Publish to github pages 🌐
installation/github-pages.text: Publish to github pages 🌐 The most common use for papiro is to publish it as a github page. Create a github repository Create a github repository for your documents and enable the github pages feature following the official guide. Upload your files to a directory inside your repository and install the official papiro github action. Configure papiro deploy action Create a publish-docs.yaml file inside the .github/workflows directory with the following configuration: name: Publish documents on: push: branches: [main] permissions: contents: write jobs: build: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v5 - uses: akrck02/papiro-deploy@main with: title: "title" # your project title description: "description" # your project description logo: "./logo.svg" # your logo path (only svg for now) accent: "#2BB3A3" # your project's colour, adjusted for light and dark width: "normal" # "wide" for pages as wide as the screen path: "./your-docs-path" # the file with your markdown documents isObsidianProject: false # if it is an obsidian project showFooter: true # if the footer of the page must be shown showBreadcrumb: true # if the breadcrumb of the page must be shown showStartPage: true # if the start page must be shown - name: Deploy to github actions 🚀 uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4 # please checkout and give a star to this amazing action. with: branch: gh-pages # The branch the action should deploy to. folder: . # The folder the action should deploy. This workflow will download the latest version of papiro, convert and index your documents and deploy the website to a branch called gh-pages in your repository. ⚠️ Make sure that the actions can write into the repository and that the gh-pages branch is used as github pages branch in the configuration Congratulations 🎉🎉 --- your wiki is now ready to visit in yourusername.github.io/your-project or your custom github domain ---

installation/local-testing.title: Local testing 🧪
installation/local-testing.text: Local testing 🧪 Download the latest papiro version from the official github repository. and enter its directory. cd ./papiro Then preview any folder of markdown documents, or an Obsidian vault: ./bin/preview.sh ~/notes/my-vault The script builds papiro, indexes your documents (Obsidian vaults are detected by their .obsidian folder) and serves the wiki locally. It only needs python3, and go on systems other than linux x86-64, where it builds esbuild and the papiro indexer the first time. Once done, the web will be launched in the following URL. http://127.0.0.1:8000 Run the script again after changing your documents, or pass another port as the second argument. Congratulations 🎉🎉 --- your wiki is now ready to visit in the local environment. ---
